newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ex-Venezuelan premier sees trade battle with Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Venezuelan premier sees trade battle with Colombia.

text.p: Former Venezuelan president Carlos Andres Perez warned finance industry heads in Bogota Thursday that trade disputes were driving Colombia and Venezuela to open confrontation.

The ex-premier, in his first public address abroad since his release from house arrest on corruption charges in September, criticised the two neighbouring governments for the battle that flared mid-way in September over imports of Colombian sugar to Venezuela.

He called on Colombia and Venezuela's other Andean Pact partners, Bolivia, Ecuador and Peru, to work together on Latin American economic integration instead of negotiating bilateral accords with other nations in the region.

The Andean Pact cannot continue being half free trade zone and half customs union. We must resolve this dilemma with the aim of working towards amore integrated and more democratic Latin America," Perez said.

Perez went on to warn that there was still a latent threat of social turmoil in his native venezuela. His administration was hit by widespread riots in February 1989 in the wake of an austere economic stabilzation package.
He added that the booming popularity of former Miss Universe- turned-mayoress Irene Saez was a clear sign of grassroots disenchantment with the established political parties in Venezuela.

According to recent opinion polls in Venezuela, Saez, currently mayoress of the Venezuelan city of Chacao, would win presidential elections if these were held now. She has not said if she will run for the post.
